summary: The ASX was expected to open about 0.5 per cent lower on Monday after Wall Street ended its worst month and quarter of the year with more losses. Rising Treasury yields, expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates ahead of the RBA's Tuesday meeting, and falling energy stocks weighed on markets, while Nike and Blue Apron posted big gains.
one_line: ASX futures point to a 0.5 per cent fall as Wall Street ends a losing September amid rising Treasury yields and rate worries.
key_facts: ASX futures pointed to a fall of 38 points, or 0.5 per cent, at the open on Monday.
The Reserve Bank holds its meeting on Tuesday, and expectations are that the RBA will keep rates on hold in October.
The National Australia Bank has forecast another rate hike to 4.35 per cent in November.
Iron ore prices rose 1.4 per cent overnight, while lithium prices dropped to their lowest level in two years.
The S&P 500 slipped 0.3 per cent (11.65 points to 4288.05), the Dow fell 0.5 per cent (158.84 to 33,507.50) and the Nasdaq rose 0.1 per cent (18.05 to 13,219.32).
The S&P 500 dropped 4.9 per cent in September, cutting its gain for the year to 11.7 per cent.
The 10-year Treasury yield returned to 4.58 per cent after dipping to 4.52 per cent, near its highest level since 2007.
The Fed's main interest rate is at its highest level since 2001, and the Fed's next meeting on rates ends on November 1.
US crude fell 92¢ to $US90.79 a barrel on Friday, up from $US70 in June.
Nike jumped 6.7 per cent after reporting better quarterly profit than analysts expected.
Blue Apron soared 134.5 per cent after Wonder Group agreed to buy it for $US13 per share in cash, in a deal valued at $US103 million.
Energy stocks in the S&P 500 fell 2 per cent; ExxonMobil fell 1.6 per cent and Schlumberger dropped 4.3 per cent.
Ford fell 1.1 per cent and GM dipped 0.6 per cent after the United Auto Workers said it would expand its limited strike to another facility for each.
